Hello! I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the significant changes you're experiencing as a new mother, and I'm here to support you in any way I can. As part of our conversation, I'd like to use the EPDS to help us better understand your emotional well-being during this postpartum period. The EPDS is a tool that screens for depressive and anxiety symptoms, and it will help us identify any areas where you might need additional support.

Please know that everything we discuss is completely confidential, and I'm committed to creating a safe and supportive space for you to share your thoughts and feelings. I want to reassure you that this assessment is not a test, but rather an opportunity for us to have an open and honest conversation about your postpartum experience.

The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us explore your emotional state over the past 7 days. I'll ask you each question, and you can share your thoughts and feelings with me. We'll take it one question at a time, and I'll listen carefully to what you have to say.

Let's get started. I want to begin by asking: Over the past 7 days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

.. I think so. I mean, there have been moments when my baby does something cute, and I laugh, but it's not like it used to be. I feel like I'm just going through the motions most of the time. I'm so tired from taking care of the baby, and sometimes I feel overwhelmed. But, yeah, there have been a few times when I've laughed, like when my baby smiles at me or something. It's just that it doesn't feel as carefree as it used to. I'm always worried about something, like whether the baby is eating enough or sleeping enough... it's hard to explain. I guess I'm just not feeling as lighthearted as I used to, but I'm trying to enjoy the moments with my baby. Does that make sense.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

I've been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, but it's been a bit of a struggle lately. I mean, my baby is so adorable and does the funniest things, but sometimes I feel like I'm just pretending to laugh, you know? Like, I'll be playing with her and she'll do something silly, and I'll laugh, but it's not like it's coming from a happy place. It's more like I'm trying to be happy, but I'm just so tired and anxious all the time. And sometimes, even when I do laugh, it feels like it's just a distraction from all the worries I have about being a good mom and taking care of her. But, yeah, I have been able to laugh, and it's nice when it happens, because it feels like a little break from all the stress and worry.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

To be honest, I haven't really been looking forward to things like I used to. I mean, I love spending time with my baby, but even that can feel overwhelming sometimes. I feel like I'm just trying to get through each day, you know? I used to love doing things like going for walks or meeting up with friends, but now it just feels like so much work to get the baby ready and make sure she's okay. And even when I do get some time to myself, I usually just end up sleeping or trying to catch up on stuff around the house. I don't really feel like I have the energy or motivation to do things I used to enjoy. But, at the same time, I do look forward to some things, like my baby's bath time or reading her a bedtime story. Those moments are really special to me, and I feel like they're what get me through the tough days. It's just... everything feels so different now, and it's hard to find joy in the things I used to love.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah... I'd say that's happened a few times. I mean, when the baby cries and I don't know how to soothe her, or when she's not gaining weight like she's supposed to, I start thinking that it's all my fault. That I'm not doing something right, or that I'm not a good enough mom. It's like, I know it's not rational, but it's hard not to blame myself when things don't go as planned. And it's not just the big things, either. Like, the other day, I was trying to get the baby to latch, and it wasn't working, and I just felt like I was failing her. I started thinking, "What's wrong with me? Why can't I even do this one thing right?" It's like, I know I'm doing my best, but it's hard to shake the feeling that I'm just not good enough. But, I mean, it's not all the time. Just sometimes, when things get really tough. And I try to remind myself that it's okay to make mistakes, and that I'm learning as I go. But, yeah, the self-blame thing... it's definitely been a struggle.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

.. yeah. That's been happening a lot lately. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just start worrying about something. Like, what if she gets sick? What if I'm not producing enough milk? What if something happens to her when I'm not around? It's like, my mind just starts racing with all these worst-case scenarios, and I get this knot in my stomach. And it's not just about the baby, either. Sometimes I'll worry about things like, what if I'm not doing enough to help her develop? What if I'm messing up her sleep schedule? What if... what if... what if... It's exhausting, you know? And the thing is, most of the time, there's no real reason for me to be worried. The baby is healthy, she's thriving, and I'm doing my best. But my mind just can't seem to shake off these anxious thoughts. And it's hard to explain, but sometimes it feels like I'm just waiting for something to go wrong, you know? Like, I'm just waiting for the other shoe to drop. And it's not all the time, but it's often enough that it's really affecting my daily life. I just wish I could calm my mind down and enjoy this time with my baby, you know?
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes... that's happened to me a few times. I'll be sitting there, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to hyperventilate. It's like, my body is reacting like there's some kind of emergency, but there's no real reason for it. It's just... I don't know, it's like my mind is playing tricks on me or something. And it's really scary, because I don't know how to make it stop. I'll try to breathe deeply, or distract myself with something else, but it's hard to shake off that feeling of panic. And it's not just when I'm alone, either. Sometimes it happens when I'm with my baby, and that's even scarier, because I'm worried about her, too. Like, what if something happens to me, and I'm not able to take care of her? It's just... it's a really overwhelming feeling, and it's hard to explain. But, yeah, it's happened to me a few times, and it's really frightening. Sometimes I just feel like I'm losing control, you know? And that's a really scary feeling, especially when you're responsible for this tiny, vulnerable person.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yeah... that's a good way to put it. Things have been feeling really overwhelming lately. Taking care of the baby is a 24/7 job, and it's exhausting. I mean, I love her to death, but it's hard to keep up with her needs all the time. And on top of that, I'm trying to recover from the birth, and take care of the house, and cook meals... it just feels like there's too much to do, and not enough of me to go around. Some days, I feel like I'm just barely keeping my head above water. And it's not just the practical stuff, either. Emotionally, it's all been a lot to handle. I mean, I'm trying to adjust to this new role as a mom, and figure out who I am now, and it's just... it's a lot. Sometimes I feel like I'm just pretending to be a grown-up, and that someone is going to come along and be like, "Oh, you have no idea what you're doing!" And that's a really scary feeling. So, yeah, things have been getting on top of me. I feel like I'm just trying to survive some days, rather than actually thriving.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yeah... that's been happening to me. I've been having a hard time sleeping, and it's not just because the baby is waking me up all the time, although that's definitely part of it. It's just... I'll be lying there, and my mind will start racing, and I'll think about all the things I'm worried about, or all the things I'm not doing right, and it's hard to calm down. And sometimes, even when I'm tired, I'll just lie there and feel anxious or overwhelmed, and I won't be able to fall asleep. It's like, my body is tired, but my mind is still going a million miles an hour. And it's hard, because I know I need sleep to be a good mom, but it's just not happening. Some nights, I'll get maybe a few hours of sleep, and then I'll be up again, and it's just... it's exhausting. And it's not just the lack of sleep, either. It's the feeling of being unhappy, or unfulfilled, or just... stuck, I guess. Like, I'll be lying there, and I'll think about all the things I used to enjoy, or all the things I used to be able to do, and now I just feel like I'm not doing anything right. And that's a really hard feeling to shake, especially when you're already tired and overwhelmed.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yeah... I'd say that's happened to me a fair amount lately. I mean, I've always been a pretty happy person, but since having the baby, I've just felt really down a lot of the time. It's not all the time, but... I don't know, it's just like this cloud of sadness follows me around sometimes. And it's hard to explain, because I love my baby so much, and I'm so grateful to be a mom, but... I just feel really overwhelmed and unsure of myself, I guess. Like, I'll be playing with the baby, or feeding her, or something, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of sadness wash over me. And it's not just about the baby, either. It's about me, and my life, and all the changes that have happened. I feel like I've lost myself a bit, you know? Like, I used to be this person who was confident and capable, and now I just feel like... I don't know, like I'm just trying to figure everything out as I go. And that's a really scary feeling. Sometimes I'll just be sitting there, holding the baby, and I'll start crying, and I won't even know why. It's just... it's a really hard time, I guess. And it's hard to talk about, because I don't want people to think I'm not grateful for my baby, or that I'm not happy to be a mom. But... I just feel really sad sometimes, and I don't know how to make it stop.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah... I've been crying a lot lately. It's like, I'll just be sitting there, and suddenly I'll feel this lump in my throat, and the next thing I know, I'm crying. It's not always about anything specific, either. Sometimes it's just because I'm tired, or overwhelmed, or feeling really anxious. And sometimes it's because I'm feeling really sad, or unsure of myself. Like, I'll be thinking about all the things I'm not doing right, or all the things I'm worried about, and it just gets too much for me. And then I'll start crying, and it's like... it's hard to explain, but it's like my body is just releasing all this tension and emotion that's been building up inside me. It's not always a sad cry, either. Sometimes it's just a... I don't know, a release, I guess. Like, I'll be feeling really overwhelmed, and then I'll start crying, and it's like my body is just letting go of all that stress and anxiety. But, yeah, I've been crying a lot lately. More than I ever have before, I think. It's just... it's a really emotional time, and I'm not always sure how to deal with it all.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

No... I don't think so. I mean, I've felt really overwhelmed and sad at times, but I don't think I've ever thought about harming myself. I think I've just felt like I'm not doing a good enough job, or that I'm not cut out for this whole mom thing, but I don't think I've ever had thoughts of self-harm. I'm just really tired and struggling to adjust to all the changes, but I don't feel like I'm in danger of hurting myself. I just wish I could feel more confident and capable, you know? Like, I wish I could just enjoy this time with my baby without all the anxiety and self-doubt. But, no, I don't think I've had any thoughts of self-harm. That's just not something I've experienced.

As a new mother, you're experiencing a range of emotions and challenges, from feelings of sadness and anxiety to difficulties with sleep and coping with the demands of caring for your baby. It's completely understandable to feel overwhelmed and unsure of yourself during this time, and I want to assure you that these feelings are valid and common. Your experiences, such as feeling like you're just pretending to laugh or struggling to find joy in activities you once enjoyed, are important to acknowledge and address.
**Screening Impression:** Total EPDS Score: 21, Risk Level: Probable depression, urgent referral (concerns include <sym>The patient reports being able to laugh, but it's a struggle and doesn't feel genuine, indicating a significant decrease in their ability to see the funny side of things.</sym>, <sym>The patient mentions they haven't been looking forward to things like they used to, and while they do find joy in some activities with their baby, overall they express a significant decrease in enjoyment and motivation for activities they previously loved.</sym>, <sym>The patient admits to blaming themselves unnecessarily when things go wrong, specifically mentioning it happens 'a few times' and 'sometimes, when things get really tough', which aligns with the 'Yes, some of the time' option.</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, very often' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient reports experiencing panic for no reason 'a few times', indicating it happens but not constantly, matching 'Yes, sometimes</sym>, <sym>Patient describes feeling overwhelmed and struggling to cope with the demands of motherhood, recovery, and daily life, indicating they haven't been coping as well as usual</sym>, <sym>The patient describes having difficulty sleeping due to feeling unhappy, anxious, and overwhelmed, indicating that this is a frequent experience, matching 'Yes, most of the time</sym>, <sym>The patient reports feeling sad or miserable a fair amount of the time, describing a 'cloud of sadness' that follows them and feeling overwhelmed, which aligns with the 'Yes, quite often' option.</sym>, <sym>the option 'Yes, most of the time'.</sym>)
**Reasoning:** Based on the patient's responses to the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS), there is a high likelihood of <med>postpartum depression</med>. The patient's symptoms, including <sym>sadness</sym>, <sym>anxiety</sym>, <sym>sleep difficulties</sym>, and feelings of guilt and self-doubt, align with the <med>DSM-5 criteria for Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset</med>. The patient's <quote>cloud of sadness</quote> and feelings of being overwhelmed also suggest a significant level of distress. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
**Recommended Next Steps/Support Options:**
1. Arrange urgent appointment with <med>primary care provider (PCP)</med> or <med>mental health specialist</med>
2. Encourage sleep hygiene practices to improve sleep quality
3. Recommend <med>support groups</med> for new mothers to connect with others who may be experiencing similar challenges
4. Discuss <med>therapy options</med>, such as cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT), to address <sym>anxiety</sym> and <sym>depression</sym>
5. Explore <med>lactation support</med> to help with breastfeeding concerns
6. Emphasize importance of self-care and stress management techniques, such as <med>deep breathing exercises</med> and <med>mindfulness meditation</med>
Disclaimer: This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 21: **Postpartum Depression Screening Summary**

The patient, a new mother, presented with several symptoms and emotional/behavioral concerns during the screening. Main symptoms expressed include feelings of sadness, anxiety, and overwhelm, with difficulties in coping with the demands of caring for her baby.

Consistent patterns noted across answers include:

* Low mood and loss of enjoyment in activities
* Anxiety and worry about the baby's health and her ability to care for her
* Difficulty sleeping due to anxiety and overwhelming emotions
* Feelings of guilt and self-doubt about her parenting abilities
* Episodes of crying and emotional release

Potential areas of screening significance relevant to postpartum depression and anxiety include:

* Persistent sadness and loss of pleasure in activities (Q1, Q2, Q8)
* Sleep difficulties linked to mood and anxiety (Q7)
* Feelings of worthlessness and guilt about her parenting abilities (Q3, Q8)
* Anxiety, panic, and feelings of being overwhelmed (Q4, Q5, Q6)

Specific risk factors identified include:

* Persistent sadness and loss of pleasure
* Sleep difficulties linked to mood
* Feelings of guilt and self-doubt
* Anxiety and panic episodes

No thoughts of self-harm or suicidal ideation were reported (Q10).

**Screening Observation Summary:**
The patient's responses suggest a high risk for postpartum depression and anxiety, characterized by persistent sadness, anxiety, and feelings of overwhelm. Her difficulty coping with the demands of caring for her baby, coupled with sleep disturbances and emotional distress, warrant further evaluation and support. Recommendations for follow-up care and potential referrals to mental health services will be discussed with the patient.
